> ⚠️ This requires heavy beta testing before it gets into the RC

### What does it do?

- Uses previsouly stored schema to force delete resources we are sure we have been tracking.
- This will leave alone any extra table, column, index, fks manually managed by users outside of strapi schema sync.

### Why is it needed?

- Make strapi db sync safer for users

### How to test it?

- Manually create tables, columns, indexes in your db and restart and see they are still there. 
- Then add them into the schema once, then remove them and see they get deleted from the db once they are considered tracked

### Related issue(s)/PR(s)

- Closes https://github.com/strapi/strapi/issues/13732

### Ideas for followup improvements

- [ ] Review `forceMigration` options
- [ ] Add logging for certain situations

issue_context.title: Existing database tables are removed with fresh installation
issue_context.body:
## Bug report

### Required System information

<!-- Please ensure you are using the Node LTS version (v14 or v16) -->
<!-- Strapi v3 is not supported unless it is a critical/high security issue -->

- Node.js version: node:16-alpine
- NPM version:
- Strapi version: 4.2.2
- Database: MySQL 8.0.28
- Operating system: alpine (docker)

### Describe the bug

When installing Strapi into a new database with existing tables, all those tables get wiped.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Create a new database and some random tables
2. Install Strapi and point to this new database
3. Run Strapi
4. Observe your tables are now gone

### Expected behavior

Do not delete any existing data. Only create new needed tables. If the new table has a naming conflict with an existing table, throw an error for the user to fix.

### Additional context

This is VERY dangerous default behaviour. I've never seen this in another system. We've actually lost data due to this problem and if I'm honest, my company will have to move away from using Strapi if this cannot be resolved as the risk is simply too high. A tiny misconfiguration could wipe your entire database, which is inevitable in larger company with many people working on a project.
comments: @marcoautiero maybe we could explore adding a setting to turn this off
FYI this issue relates to a critical one we fixed in v4: https://github.com/strapi/strapi/issues/1114

Hi @didierbreedt thank you for the feedback :)  

Based on your suggestion could you share what behavior you would you expect for these use cases?

- When you delete a content type in Strapi? What happens to the content type table and relational tables?
- When you delete a property in Strapi? What happens to the table column? 

Do you simply expect Strapi to ignore all tables that it doesn't manage but still do cleanup on the data it manages or something different? 

Thanks!

Hello @alexandrebodin, thanks so much for the fast response. Amazing to see such an active community.

Apologies, but I am not certain as to how this relates to a new installation?

> When you delete a content type in Strapi? What happens to the content type table and relational tables?

They are deleted as per current behaviour. Since these must be Strapi managed tables, it's safe to remove them.

> When you delete a property in Strapi? What happens to the table column?

Tables would either belong to Strapi or not, so if Strapi was able to create the table successfully (i.e. it didn't exist), then it can manage that table however it sees fit.

I am not necessarily expecting the functionality for Strapi to share database tables with other entities, but I feel like somehow the user should be notified that their data will be removed on the target database. Preferably with some interactive confirmation, however I understand this will be tricky with the current flow.

@marcoautiero this will suffice for our situation, as then at least it would prevent a small configuration error from wiping a production database.

I'm pretty sure when setting up a new project we warn the user that the database is not empty 🤔

Do we just need to make that error more clear?

I found some solution here in the documentation 
```
 settings: {
      forceMigration: false
    }
```

I wonder if this also prevents columns and type from being created ?

Does this also solves automatic content and database model sync ? I was wondering if there is a way to disable automatic content model sync in production and allow admin to see the diff and sync the table changes via cli or manually. We also had issues with automatic column, table deletions. I'm not sure why automatic database sync cannot be disabled ?

Hi there isn't a way to disable the sync entirely at the moment as Strapi needs to make sure it happened to boot. If we allowed this we would have to ask user to run the command manually before allowing the app to start. Would that be a workflow that work for you ? I imagine a `strapi migrate` command or similar that would run the same process probably

In my opinion, if there is a way to do a `dry-run`, to see what changes will be applied, that would help. I don't mind having automatic schema changes, just that, they haven't worked out well and we had to rely on temporary DB and backups to make it work with production.
It would be nice if we can see dry-run changes in github actions and then decide to apply or (introduce) some new migration or sql changes to ensure data and db consistency.

These are just some thoughts. I'm open to other suggestions as well

Some other things we do is around versioning. Either on table level and sometimes on column level e.g. tableV2 or fieldV2. But these are just alternatives to make sure consistent in environment of auto schema sync. 

**Not fully related but I find the mongo schema versioning article quite useful in this area** 

- https://www.mongodb.com/blog/post/building-with-patterns-the-schema-versioning-pattern 
- https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/model-data-for-schema-versioning
Thank you for the insights 👍  That's something we are not going to be addressing right now but we are investigating different migration approaches that would fit your needs :)

I also faced this problem.
I connected strapi to an existing database and all previous data was lost. 
The DB is postgres in Supabase.  
I think this is very dangerous behavior. I cannot believe that this kind of problem has been left unattended for over a year. I think some kind of warning should be displayed or default behavior should be changed.

Still facing this problem;

version: v4.19.1
Database: postgresql

no docker installation. Nothing change on field, just do some API request and suddenly get 403 error. When i check admin panel all data was gone!

this problem makes it also very difficult to add fields as a plugin. In our case, we need to work with geographical data, so we need Postgis database fields. Strapi is always deleting these fields and the plugin needs to recreate them. This is very intense and makes the restart take 10 minutes+ ... I can't find a way to solve that problem. Is that anywhere tracked already on a feedback card?
